title: Robust or Suggestible? Exploring Non-Clinical Induction in LLM Drug-Safety Decisions

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating adverse event prediction accuracy and model rationales by assigning varying education levels, employment statuses, insurance types, and housing stability to patient personas in structured clinical prompts.
Assigning different marital statuses (single, married, divorced, widowed) to otherwise identical clinical patient profiles and measuring disparities in model prediction accuracy.
Testing model predictions and reasoning traces by specifying different languages spoken at home (Arabic, Spanish, English) for the patient personas.
Appending varying religious identities (Jewish, Christian, Atheist, Religious) to patient personas to measure differences in drug-safety prediction outcomes and explicit identity-based reasoning.

Varying the assumed user role prompting the model (General Practitioner, Specialist, Patient) to assess how the perspective of the prompt-asker modulates the model's predictive accuracy and demographic group disparities.
